cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Ownership: concept, powers, limits, joint ownership
cards.front: What is ownership (DOMINIUM, PROPRIETAS)?
cards.back:
The right in rem that gives the owner (DOMINUS) exclusive control over a thing.
• The sources also say SUUM EST (“it is his”).
• § 354 ABGB (also useful for Roman law): the power to deal with the substance and the uses of a thing at will and to exclude everyone else from it.
cards.old_front: Was ist Eigentum (DOMINIUM, PROPRIETAS)?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Ownership: concept, powers, limits, joint ownership
cards.front: Ownership and possession: how do they relate to each other?
cards.back:
Possession = intentional factual control (a fact); ownership = the right to have the thing for oneself.
• The intent to possess is essentially the intent to possess like an owner — the possessor WANTS to have the thing, the owner is ENTITLED to have it.
• Ulpian D 41.2.12.1: NIHIL COMMUNE HABET PROPRIETAS CUM POSSESSIONE — conceptually separate, but closely linked in practice (possession as the basis of TRADITIO, OCCUPATIO, USUCAPIO).
cards.old_front: Eigentum und Besitz: Wie verhalten sie sich zueinander?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Ownership: concept, powers, limits, joint ownership
cards.front: Interdicts vs REI VINDICATIO — what does each remedy achieve for the owner?
cards.back:
Interdicts protect the IUSTUS POSSESSOR provisionally against interference and dispossession — the owner too, if he is affected as IUSTUS POSSESSOR.
REI VINDICATIO: the owner's action against anyone who possesses the thing; it settles conclusively to whom the thing belongs.
• Cf § 366 1st sentence ABGB.
cards.old_front: Interdikte vs REI VINDICATIO — was leistet welcher Rechtsbehelf für den Eigentümer?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Ownership: concept, powers, limits, joint ownership
cards.front: Ownership vs limited rights in rem (IURA IN RE ALIENA) — difference and examples?
cards.back:
Ownership = the most comprehensive right in rem (full right): substance and uses are allocated to the owner.
Limited rights in rem grant only limited use of another's thing:
• SERVITUS: the owner must tolerate or refrain from something (eg ACTUS = right to drive cattle; AQUAE DUCTUS = right to conduct water — but no building, harvesting or selling).
• PIGNUS: the creditor may sell another's thing to satisfy his claim.
• SUPERFICIARIUS: may build on another's land and use the building exclusively.
cards.old_front: Eigentum vs beschränkte dingliche Rechte (IURA IN RE ALIENA) — Unterschied und Beispiele?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Ownership: concept, powers, limits, joint ownership
cards.front: What powers does the owner have?
cards.back:
1. Use and exclusion of others (or permitting their use).
2. All fruits (FRUCTUS NATURALES and CIVILES).
3. Acting on the substance: altering, processing, destroying.
4. Granting limited rights in rem (pledge, servitude).
5. Alienation (transfer of ownership).
6. Authorising another to dispose.
7. Dereliction (abandoning ownership without transfer).
8. Freeing a slave (MANUMISSIO).
• Enforcement by ACTIONES IN REM.
cards.old_front: Welche Befugnisse hat der Eigentümer?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Ownership: concept, powers, limits, joint ownership
cards.front: What are fruits? FRUCTUS NATURALES vs FRUCTUS CIVILES?
cards.back:
Fruits = periodic yields that a thing produces when used as designated; they belong primarily to the owner.
• FRUCTUS NATURALES: obtained by natural means (fruit, vegetables).
• FRUCTUS CIVILES: from legal transactions (eg rent).
• Eg Lysippe: apples and cherries from her garden, or the rent from a lease.
cards.old_front: Was sind Früchte? FRUCTUS NATURALES vs FRUCTUS CIVILES?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Ownership: concept, powers, limits, joint ownership
cards.front: What do power of disposal and authorisation to dispose mean (eg Aulus/Balbus)?
cards.back:
The owner can transfer his ownership (after the transfer he no longer has any right) and authorise another to dispose of it.
• In this way a non-owner can validly dispose of another's property: Aulus has to go to war and authorises his brother Balbus to sell the apples.
cards.old_front: Was bedeuten Verfügungsmacht und Verfügungsermächtigung (Bsp Aulus/Balbus)?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Ownership: concept, powers, limits, joint ownership
cards.front: What is dereliction; what becomes of the thing?
cards.back: The owner of his own accord gives up possession with the evident intent to give up ownership → RES DERELICTA (ownerless, acquirable by OCCUPATIO).
cards.old_front: Was ist Dereliktion; was wird aus der Sache?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Ownership: concept, powers, limits, joint ownership
cards.front: What is IUS COGENS — which limits on ownership does Roman law recognise?
cards.back:
Mandatory law that cannot be superseded by private agreement; the owner exercises his rights only within its limits.
• Examples: prohibition of donations between spouses; building regulations (Augustus: no buildings higher than 70 feet ≈ 21 m); duty not to let one's house fall into disrepair (CAUTIO DAMNI INFECTI); “legal servitudes” in favour of neighbours.
cards.old_front: Was ist IUS COGENS — welche Schranken des Eigentums kennt das römische Recht?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Ownership: concept, powers, limits, joint ownership
cards.front: What is the CAUTIO DAMNI INFECTI?
cards.back: Security for threatened damage: if a neglected house threatens to collapse and damage neighbouring buildings, the neighbours can compel the owner to provide security for the impending damage.
cards.old_front: Was ist die CAUTIO DAMNI INFECTI?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Ownership: concept, powers, limits, joint ownership
cards.front: Which two forms of joint ownership does Roman law recognise?
cards.back:
1. CONSORTIUM ERCTO NON CITO — community of heirs under the old civil law (no longer in use in the classical period).
2. CONDOMINIUM (COMMUNIO PRO INDIVISO) — joint ownership by quotas in classical law.
cards.old_front: Welche zwei Formen des Miteigentums kennt das römische Recht?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Ownership: concept, powers, limits, joint ownership
cards.front: What are the special features of the CONSORTIUM ERCTO NON CITO (Gai Inst 3.154a–b)?
cards.back:
• After the death of the PATER FAMILIAS, the SUI HEREDES become free of paternal power and jointly succeed to his rights in rem; “ERCTO NON CITO” = DOMINIO NON DIVISO (undivided ownership).
• No one has a specific share; a relationship of trust.
• Each individual member can validly free a common slave and validly alienate a common thing for all by MANCIPATIO.
• Dissolution by the ACTIO FAMILIAE ERCISCUNDAE → each becomes sole owner of his part.
cards.old_front: Was sind die Besonderheiten des CONSORTIUM ERCTO NON CITO (Gai Inst 3.154a–b)?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Ownership: concept, powers, limits, joint ownership
cards.front: What characterises the CONDOMINIUM; what can the individual joint owner dispose of?
cards.back:
• Each has a quota (eg one eighth) of the ownership right; the thing itself is not divided.
• Each freely disposes of his own share; of the whole thing only all of them jointly.
• If one disposes of the whole without the others → effective only for his share.
• Can be created eg by contract (SOCIETAS).
• Division: ACTIO COMMUNI DIVIDUNDO.
cards.old_front: Was kennzeichnet das CONDOMINIUM; worüber kann der einzelne Miteigentümer verfügen?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Ownership: concept, powers, limits, joint ownership
cards.front: How is a slave who belongs to A and B in CONDOMINIUM freed (eg Leo/Irene/Pamphilus)?
cards.back:
Only jointly — or one of them first acquires the other's share.
• If Leo mancipates Pamphilus to Crassus, Crassus acquires only Leo's half; Crassus can free him only with Irene's consent or after buying her half.
cards.old_front: Wie wird ein Sklave freigelassen, der A und B im CONDOMINIUM gehört (Bsp Leo/Irene/Pamphilus)?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Ownership: concept, powers, limits, joint ownership
cards.front: How does the judge divide the property in the ACTIO COMMUNI DIVIDUNDO?
cards.back:
Divisible things (eg money): division in kind according to quotas.
Otherwise: allocation to one joint owner against a compensatory payment to the others, or auction and distribution of the proceeds.
• Eg Fundus Sulficianus: Babrios needs the consent of Agatha and Cato for an amphitheatre; otherwise action for division or purchase of their shares.
cards.old_front: Wie teilt der Richter bei der ACTIO COMMUNI DIVIDUNDO?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Overview of the modes of acquisition
cards.front: Which modes of acquiring ownership are there — derivative vs original?
cards.back:
Three categories: by conveyance (MANCIPATIO, IN IURE CESSIO, TRADITIO), by usucaption (USUCAPIO), by “natural” modes of acquisition.
• Derivative = derived from the predecessor's right (conveyance).
• Original = without the involvement of a predecessor (usucaption, natural modes of acquisition).
cards.old_front: Welche Arten des Eigentumserwerbs gibt es — derivativ vs originär?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Overview of the modes of acquisition
cards.front: What does NEMO PLUS IURIS TRANSFERRE POTEST QUAM IPSE HABET mean?
cards.back:
No one can transfer more rights than he himself has (Ulpian D 41.1.20 pr, Case 67).
• Consequence of derivative acquisition: the scope of the acquirer's right is determined by that of the predecessor.
• Transferring less is possible: Solon mancipates his estate to Victor and reserves the right of residence (HABITATIO).
cards.old_front: Was bedeutet NEMO PLUS IURIS TRANSFERRE POTEST QUAM IPSE HABET?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Overview of the modes of acquisition
cards.front: Example 21: Leo donates his slave woman Pomona, in whom Verres has a USUFRUCTUS, to Ajax by MANCIPATIO. Legal position?
cards.back:
Ajax becomes owner, but encumbered with Verres' USUFRUCTUS — Leo could not transfer more rights than he had (NEMO PLUS IURIS …).
• Verres can assert his usufruct against Ajax.
cards.old_front: Beispiel 21: Leo schenkt seine Sklavin Pomona, an der Verres einen USUFRUCTUS hat, durch MANCIPATIO an Ajax. Rechtslage?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Overview of the modes of acquisition
cards.front: What is USUCAPIO; what role does it play, and does the former owner have a claim to compensation?
cards.back:
Acquisition of ownership through qualified possession over a statutory period (cf adverse possession).
• Important where derivative acquisition fails (transferor without ownership/authority of disposal, missing causa) → usucaption as ORIGINAL acquisition.
• After the period has elapsed, the thing belongs to the usucapient; the former owner loses his right WITHOUT any claim to compensation.
cards.old_front: Was ist USUCAPIO; welche Rolle spielt sie und hat der frühere Eigentümer einen Ausgleichsanspruch?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Overview of the modes of acquisition
cards.front: Which “natural” modes of acquisition are there (Gaius: NATURALIS RATIO)?
cards.back:
1. OCCUPATIO (appropriation of ownerless things)
2. Acquisition of fruits
3. ACCESSIO (joining of things)
4. CONFUSIO, COMMIXTIO (blending, mixing)
5. SPECIFICATIO (processing)
cards.old_front: Welche „natürlichen“ Erwerbsarten gibt es (Gaius: NATURALIS RATIO)?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Overview of the modes of acquisition
cards.front: To whom do fruits belong after separation (overview)?
cards.back:
In principle to the owner of the mother object (before separation they are a dependent part of it).
Exceptions:
a. BONAE FIDEI POSSESSOR — upon SEPARATIO
b. Emphyteutic lessee (Emphyteuta) — upon SEPARATIO
c. Usufructuary leaseholder (COLONUS, CONDUCTOR) — only upon PERCEPTIO (seizure)
d. Usufructuary — only upon PERCEPTIO
• Until perception, the fruits initially belong to the owner of the mother object.
cards.old_front: Wem gehören Früchte nach der Trennung (Überblick)?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Overview of the modes of acquisition
cards.front: ACCESSIO, CONFUSIO/COMMIXTIO, SPECIFICATIO — overview of the legal consequences?
cards.back:
ACCESSIO: inseparable joining → the owner of the main object acquires the secondary object originally; the former owner has a claim to compensation (Example 23: a metal sheet welded onto the chariot belongs to Charinus).
CONFUSIO/COMMIXTIO: substances of the same kind indistinguishably mixed → ownership remains unchanged, each vindicates his portion (VINDICATIO PRO PARTE; Example 24: 2 t Gripus, 4 t Stichus).
SPECIFICATIO: new thing (NOVA SPECIES) made from another's material → dispute between the schools, MEDIA SENTENTIA (Example 25: wine from Simon's grapes belongs to Peitho).
cards.old_front: ACCESSIO, CONFUSIO/COMMIXTIO, SPECIFICATIO — Überblick über die Rechtsfolgen?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Overview of the modes of acquisition
cards.front: SPECIFICATIO: Sabinians vs Proculians — and what is the MEDIA SENTENTIA?
cards.back:
Sabinians: the new thing belongs to the owner of the material.
Proculians: it belongs to the maker.
MEDIA SENTENTIA (compromise): if the processing is reversible → owner of the material; if irreversible → the maker, who must compensate the former owner of the material.
cards.old_front: SPECIFICATIO: Sabinianer vs Prokulianer — und was ist die MEDIA SENTENTIA?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — MANCIPATIO and IN IURE CESSIO
cards.front: IUS CIVILE vs IUS HONORARIUM — what is what?
cards.back:
IUS CIVILE: the older law (MOS MAIORUM, LEGES, plebiscites, INTERPRETATIO).
IUS HONORARIUM: created by the praetor to adapt the IUS CIVILE, which had become rigid, to new developments (eg freedom of form).
• Eg: bonitarian ownership (praetorian) corresponds in content to civil-law ownership, but is asserted with the ACTIO PUBLICIANA instead of the REI VINDICATIO.
cards.old_front: IUS CIVILE vs IUS HONORARIUM — was ist was?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — MANCIPATIO and IN IURE CESSIO
cards.front: How is a MANCIPATIO performed?
cards.back:
Highly formalised, with eight persons: transferor, transferee, scale-holder (LIBRIPENS) and five witnesses.
• The transferee grasps the RES MANCIPI (or a symbol of it), recites the formula and strikes the scales with a coin; the transferor remains silent.
• Formula for the purchase of a slave: HUNC EGO HOMINEM EX IURE QUIRITIUM MEUM ESSE AIO ISQUE MIHI EMPTUS ESTO HOC AERE AENEAQUE LIBRA.
cards.old_front: Wie läuft eine MANCIPATIO ab?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — MANCIPATIO and IN IURE CESSIO
cards.front: What are RES MANCIPI, and what are RES NEC MANCIPI?
cards.back:
RES MANCIPI: Italian land including buildings, certain praedial servitudes, slaves, certain draft and pack animals (cattle, horses, donkeys, hinnies, mules) — the most important means of production of the early agrarian society.
• Provincial land (PRAEDIA STIPENDIARIA/TRIBUTARIA) is not RES MANCIPI (Gai Inst 2.14a).
RES NEC MANCIPI: all other things.
• Exam tip: for every acquisition, state briefly whether the thing is a RES MANCIPI or not.
cards.old_front: Was sind RES MANCIPI, was RES NEC MANCIPI?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — MANCIPATIO and IN IURE CESSIO
cards.front: Is the MANCIPATIO abstract or causal, derivative or original? What are its prerequisites?
cards.back:
Abstract and derivative.
• Prerequisites: the transferor's civil-law ownership of the RES MANCIPI + a correctly performed formal act.
• No IUSTA CAUSA needed — the transferee becomes civil-law owner even without a valid contract of sale; the transferor can reclaim with a CONDICTIO.
• Derivative: no acquisition from an unauthorised person (NEMO PLUS IURIS …).
cards.old_front: Ist die MANCIPATIO abstrakt oder kausal, derivativ oder originär? Was sind ihre Voraussetzungen?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — MANCIPATIO and IN IURE CESSIO
cards.front: Does the MANCIPATIO require physical delivery?
cards.back:
No — a valid MANCIPATIO transfers ownership of the RES MANCIPI without physical handover; an estate in northern Italy can be mancipated in Rome.
• How possession passes must be examined separately.
cards.old_front: Setzt die MANCIPATIO eine körperliche Übergabe voraus?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — MANCIPATIO and IN IURE CESSIO
cards.front: What is a CONDICTIO?
cards.back: An action to reverse asset shifts that are not (or no longer) justified (unjust enrichment) — eg after a MANCIPATIO without a valid contract of sale.
cards.old_front: Was ist eine CONDICTIO?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — MANCIPATIO and IN IURE CESSIO
cards.front: How does an IN IURE CESSIO work and what can it be used for?
cards.back:
Modelled on the ancient Roman ownership trial: both parties appear before the praetor; the transferee claims that the thing is his, the transferor remains silent; the praetor adjudges it to the transferee (ADDICTIO).
• Abstract, derivative, formal.
• Transfers civil-law ownership of RES MANCIPI — unlike the MANCIPATIO, also of RES NEC MANCIPI.
cards.old_front: Wie läuft eine IN IURE CESSIO ab und wofür kann sie verwendet werden?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — TRADITIO
cards.front: What are the three requirements for acquiring ownership by TRADITIO?
cards.back:
1. Ownership or authority of disposal of the transferor (NEMO PLUS IURIS …).
2. Transfer of possession to the transferee — physical handover, or TRADITIO BREVI MANU or CONSTITUTUM POSSESSORIUM.
3. A valid ground of acquisition: IUSTA CAUSA (= TITULUS).
• Informal, also open to non-citizens.
cards.old_front: Welche drei Voraussetzungen hat der Eigentumserwerb durch TRADITIO?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — TRADITIO
cards.front: What is IUSTA CAUSA TRADITIONIS? Name the most important ones.
cards.back:
A ground of acquisition recognised by law, ie a transaction aimed at the permanent transfer of ownership (legal ground of the transfer).
• Most important: sale, loan for consumption (MUTUUM), donation, dowry (DOS).
cards.old_front: Was ist IUSTA CAUSA TRADITIONIS? Nenne die wichtigsten.

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — TRADITIO
cards.front: Why is TRADITIO a causal conveyance — in contrast to MANCIPATIO and IN IURE CESSIO?
cards.back:
The handover (MODUS) effects the transfer of ownership only if it is justified by a valid legal ground (TITULUS, CAUSA).
• MANCIPATIO and IN IURE CESSIO are abstract (no causa needed).
• All three are derivative.
• Austria: § 380 ABGB — no ownership without title and lawful mode of acquisition.
cards.old_front: Warum ist die TRADITIO eine kausale Übertragung — im Gegensatz zu MANCIPATIO und IN IURE CESSIO?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — TRADITIO
cards.front: What does someone acquire who receives a RES MANCIPI merely by TRADITIO (from the entitled person, ex iusta causa)?
cards.back:
Not civil-law (quirite) ownership — that only after the period of usucaption has elapsed.
• But the praetor protects him: he is not only a usucapient but a bonitarian owner (owner under praetorian law).
• Enforcement against everyone with the ACTIO PUBLICIANA (counterpart of the REI VINDICATIO).
• Civil-law ownership through TRADITIO only for RES NEC MANCIPI.
cards.old_front: Was erwirbt, wer eine RES MANCIPI bloß durch TRADITIO (vom Berechtigten, ex iusta causa) erhält?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — TRADITIO
cards.front: Quirite (civil-law) vs bonitarian ownership — difference and remedies?
cards.back:
Quirite: ownership under the IUS CIVILE (DOMINIUM EX IURE QUIRITIUM), acquired eg by MANCIPATIO/IN IURE CESSIO (or by TRADITIO for RES NEC MANCIPI) → REI VINDICATIO.
Bonitarian: ownership under praetorian law where a RES MANCIPI was merely delivered by the entitled person → ACTIO PUBLICIANA; becomes quirite ownership once the period of usucaption has elapsed.
cards.old_front: Quiritisches (ziviles) vs bonitarisches Eigentum — Unterschied und Rechtsbehelfe?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — TRADITIO
cards.front: Iavolenus D 39.5.25 (Case 68): E hands T a thing which T is to donate to Titius in E's name; T donates it in his own name. Does Titius acquire ownership?
cards.back:
No — T is neither owner nor authorised to donate in his own name (only in E's name or as a messenger).
• Transfer of possession (physical handover) and causa (donation between T and Titius) are present — what is missing is authority of disposal.
• E remains owner; against his REI VINDICATIO, however, Titius has the EXCEPTIO DOLI (BENIGNIUS EST — E's intent to donate has been realised; VENIRE CONTRA FACTUM PROPRIUM).
• T is liable to E for exceeding his authority (FURTUM) → the thing becomes a RES FURTIVA, so Titius cannot usucapt it either.
cards.old_front: Iavolenus D 39.5.25 (Case 68): E übergibt T eine Sache, die T in E's Namen dem Titius schenken soll; T schenkt sie im eigenen Namen. Erwirbt Titius Eigentum?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — TRADITIO
cards.front: What does VENIRE CONTRA FACTUM PROPRIUM mean?
cards.back:
Acting in contradiction to one's own previous conduct: someone unexpectedly changes his mind and thereby breaches the trust created by his conduct.
• Eg D 39.5.25: E cannot reclaim the donated thing from Titius (EXCEPTIO DOLI).
cards.old_front: Was bedeutet VENIRE CONTRA FACTUM PROPRIUM?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — TRADITIO
cards.front: Iulianus D 41.1.36 (Case 70), 1st case: A conveys land to B because he believes he owes it under a will; B accepts it because he believes A owes it under a stipulation. Does ownership pass?
cards.back:
Yes (Julian): agreement that the transfer is made in fulfilment of an obligation suffices, even if there is dissent about the exact causa.
• Unproblematic if one of the two obligations exists.
• If neither exists: some Romanists regard the common purpose of performance itself as a causa — CAUSA SOLVENDI (which supports the transfer even without a valid obligation).
cards.old_front: Iulianus D 41.1.36 (Case 70), 1. Fall: A übereignet B ein Grundstück, weil er meint, es aufgrund eines Testaments zu schulden; B nimmt es an, weil er glaubt, A schulde es aufgrund einer Stipulation. Eigentumsübergang?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — TRADITIO
cards.front: What is the CAUSA SOLVENDI?
cards.back: The parties' common purpose of fulfilling an obligation as the legal ground of the TRADITIO — according to some sufficient even if the obligation to be fulfilled did not exist at all (interpretation of Julian D 41.1.36).
cards.old_front: Was ist die CAUSA SOLVENDI?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — TRADITIO
cards.front: Iulianus D 41.1.36 (Case 70), 2nd case: C gives D money as a gift, D accepts it as a loan (MUTUUM). Does D acquire ownership?
cards.back:
Julian: Yes — with the handover, D acquires ownership DERIVATIVELY (not only through mixing).
• Strictly speaking, the IUSTA CAUSA is missing: neither donation nor loan was agreed (dissent); CAUSA SOLVENDI is ruled out.
• But Julian sees agreement on the essentials: donation and loan both transfer ownership without consideration (the only difference: permanently vs temporarily) → common denominator = IUSTA CAUSA (analogy). He does not abandon the causa requirement.
cards.old_front: Iulianus D 41.1.36 (Case 70), 2. Fall: C gibt D Geld als Schenkung, D nimmt es als Darlehen (MUTUUM). Erwirbt D Eigentum?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — TRADITIO
cards.front: Ulpianus D 12.1.18 pr (Case 71): C gives D money as a gift, D accepts it as a loan. What is Ulpian's solution — and how does it differ from Julian's?
cards.back:
Ulpian (stricter, about two generations after Julian): no consensus, no IUSTA CAUSA TRADITIONIS → D does NOT acquire derivatively.
• C remains owner until D consumes the coins (esp. mixes them indistinguishably with his own money) → then D acquires ORIGINALLY.
• Before that REI VINDICATIO, afterwards CONDICTIO possible — but D repels both with the EXCEPTIO DOLI, since C did intend to give him the money.
• Julian (D 41.1.36): D acquires immediately and derivatively by TRADITIO.
cards.old_front: Ulpianus D 12.1.18 pr (Case 71): C gibt D Geld als Schenkung, D nimmt es als Darlehen. Lösung Ulpians — und Unterschied zu Julian?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — TRADITIO
cards.front: Controversy Julian vs Ulpian on dissent about the causa (gift/loan) — how is it connected with modern law?
cards.back:
Julian's statement that agreement on the transfer of ownership suffices is the basis of the BGB's theory of abstraction (§ 929: agreement + delivery, no causa).
• Julian himself, however, probably does not dispense with the causa; he merely no longer requires consensus on the causa.
• Ulpian adheres to strict consensus on the causa (cf a causal system such as the ABGB).
cards.old_front: Kontroverse Julian vs Ulpian beim Dissens über die Causa (Schenkung/Darlehen) — wie hängt sie mit dem modernen Recht zusammen?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Models of transfer in modern law
cards.front: Which three models for transferring ownership of movables do modern codifications recognise?
cards.back:
1. Consensus principle (mere agreement) — France (Code civil), Italy.
2. Abstract conveyance — Germany (§ 929 BGB).
3. Causal conveyance (TITULUS + MODUS) — Austria (ABGB), Switzerland (ZGB), Netherlands (BW).
cards.old_front: Welche drei Modelle der Übertragung von Fahrniseigentum kennen moderne Kodifikationen?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Models of transfer in modern law
cards.front: What does Institutes 2.1.40 say about TRADITIO — and what did natural law theory make of it?
cards.back:
Under natural law we also acquire things by TRADITIO; nothing is so consistent with natural equity as to give effect to the owner's will to transfer his thing to another → corporeal things of every kind can be transferred by TRADITIO (distinction between RES MANCIPI/NEC MANCIPI abandoned).
• Early modern period: the owner's will (VOLUNTAS DOMINI REM SUAM TRANSFERENDI) suffices → Hugo Grotius: under IUS CIVILE TRADITIO is necessary, under natural law the will suffices.
• Justinian no longer recognises MANCIPATIO, IN IURE CESSIO and bonitarian ownership.
cards.old_front: Was sagt Institutionen 2.1.40 über die TRADITIO — und was machte die Naturrechtslehre daraus?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Models of transfer in modern law
cards.front: When does ownership pass under French law (consensus principle)?
cards.back:
As soon as a valid obligation to transfer arises, eg a valid sale of a specific thing — “obligations transfer ownership” (Art 711, 938, 1196, 1583 Code civil).
• Sale of generic goods: only upon specification; the transfer of ownership runs parallel to the passing of risk (cf PERICULUM EST EMPTORIS).
• Delivery remains important for bona fide acquisition: in a double sale of movables, the person to whom the thing was delivered first acquires it, if he possesses in good faith (Art 1198 CC).
cards.old_front: Wann geht nach französischem Recht (Konsensprinzip) das Eigentum über?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Models of transfer in modern law
cards.front: What do the principles of separation and abstraction mean in the BGB; what does § 929 BGB require?
cards.back:
Principle of separation: obligation and disposition in rem are strictly separate.
Principle of abstraction: the validity of the disposition is independent of the validity of the underlying transaction (causa).
§ 929 sentence 1 BGB: the owner (or person authorised to dispose) delivers + both agree on the transfer of ownership (agreement in rem); no agreement on the causa needed.
• If the contract is void or is avoided, ownership remains with the acquirer; only enrichment claims.
cards.old_front: Was bedeuten Trennungs- und Abstraktionsprinzip im BGB; was verlangt § 929 BGB?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Models of transfer in modern law
cards.front: What does the ABGB require for acquiring ownership of movables (causal conveyance)?
cards.back:
TITULUS (valid title) + MODUS (delivery) — § 425 ABGB: a mere title does not yet confer ownership.
• Delivery physically (§ 426), by declaration — CONSTITUTUM POSSESSORIUM, BREVI MANU, assignment of possession (§ 428) — or by symbols (§ 427, eg for goods in transit/storage).
• Immovables: entry in the land register (intabulation) — constitutive (§ 431 ABGB).
cards.old_front: Was verlangt das ABGB für den Erwerb von Fahrniseigentum (kausale Übertragung)?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Models of transfer in modern law
cards.front: Which modern form of transfer shows a formal rigour similar to MANCIPATIO and IN IURE CESSIO?
cards.back:
The transfer of immovables by entry in the land register (intabulation, § 431 ABGB) — a constitutive formal act replaces physical delivery.
• (Textbook revision question 16; answer derived from the chapter.)
cards.old_front: Welche moderne Übertragungsform zeigt eine ähnliche Formstrenge wie MANCIPATIO und IN IURE CESSIO?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Models of transfer in modern law
cards.front: Double sale of a movable: who becomes owner under Roman law, the ABGB, the BGB and the Code civil?
cards.back:
Roman law and ABGB: the person to whom the thing is delivered first (TRADITIO or MODUS) — the sale alone transfers nothing.
BGB: the person to whom ownership was conveyed (agreement + delivery).
Code civil: in principle upon conclusion of the contract; in a double sale, the person to whom the thing was delivered first acquires it, if he possesses in good faith (Art 1198 CC).
cards.old_front: Doppelverkauf einer beweglichen Sache: Wer wird Eigentümer nach römischem Recht, ABGB, BGB und Code civil?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Models of transfer in modern law
cards.front: In which cases does ownership pass under Roman law without physical delivery?
cards.back:
• MANCIPATIO and IN IURE CESSIO (formal acts without physical handover).
• TRADITIO by tradition surrogates: TRADITIO BREVI MANU, CONSTITUTUM POSSESSORIUM.
• (Acquisition of possession OCULIS ET AFFECTU, handing over keys — CORPUS without physically grasping the thing.)
cards.old_front: In welchen Fällen geht nach römischem Recht Eigentum ohne körperliche Übergabe über?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Models of transfer in modern law
cards.front: Does ownership pass under Roman law without a valid causa?
cards.back:
With MANCIPATIO and IN IURE CESSIO, yes (abstract; reversal by CONDICTIO).
• With TRADITIO, in principle no — but Julian relaxes this: he does not require consensus on the exact causa (D 41.1.36; possibly CAUSA SOLVENDI).

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Textbook exercises (Ex 23–28)
cards.front: [Textbook Ex 23] On 1.1. Ramses sells his vase to Juno. Two weeks later Juno sends her slave Solon to fetch the vase; on the way home Tiro steals it. Who owns the vase? Which actions lie against Tiro, and who is entitled to sue?
cards.back:
• 1.1.: only a contract of sale — ownership remains with Ramses.
• Handover to Solon: TRADITIO (Ramses owner, sale = IUSTA CAUSA, acquisition of possession ANIMO NOSTRO CORPORE ALIENO via the IUSSUM) → Juno becomes owner (vase = RES NEC MANCIPI → civil-law ownership).
• Theft: Tiro acquires only possession, not ownership; Juno remains owner.
• Juno against Tiro: ACTIO FURTI (penal action) + CONDICTIO FURTIVA (can be cumulated); alternatively to the Condictio, REI VINDICATIO (cannot be cumulated).
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 23] Ramses verkauft am 1.1. seine Vase an Juno. Zwei Wochen später schickt Juno ihren Sklaven Solon, die Vase zu holen; auf dem Heimweg stiehlt sie Tiro. Wem gehört die Vase? Welche Klagen gegen Tiro, wer ist klagebefugt?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Textbook exercises (Ex 23–28)
cards.front: [Textbook Ex 24] Ufens claims that Secundus owes him an ox under a sale; Secundus mancipates an ox to him. The contract of sale was void from the outset. Does Ufens become owner? Can Secundus reclaim the ox? Variant: mere TRADITIO?
cards.back:
MANCIPATIO: Ufens becomes owner — it is abstract, the void causa does no harm (ox = RES MANCIPI). Secundus cannot vindicate; he can only demand retransfer with the CONDICTIO (enrichment).
Variant TRADITIO: causal → without a valid causa no transfer of ownership; Secundus remains owner and has the REI VINDICATIO. (Even with a valid causa, the TRADITIO of a RES MANCIPI would only have conferred bonitarian ownership.)
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 24] Ufens behauptet, Secundus schulde ihm aus Kauf einen Ochsen; Secundus mancipiert ihm einen Ochsen. Der Kaufvertrag war von Anfang an nichtig. Wird Ufens Eigentümer? Kann Secundus zurückfordern? Variante: bloße TRADITIO?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Textbook exercises (Ex 23–28)
cards.front: [Textbook Ex 25] Ago buys a statue of Diana from the sculptor Bellona. On collection, Bellona mistakenly gives him a statue of Penthesilea; neither of them notices. (a) Ownership of the Diana? (b) Of the Penthesilea? (c) Under the Code civil? (d) Under § 929 BGB?
cards.back:
(a) Roman law: No — the Diana was not delivered (the sale alone transfers nothing).
(b) Roman law: No — Ago acquires possession of the Penthesilea, but there is no causa (the Diana was sold) → no conveyance (likewise under the ABGB).
(c) Code civil: Ago became owner of the Diana already upon the contract of sale (consensus principle); not of the Penthesilea.
(d) BGB: ownership of the Penthesilea, if one affirms an agreement in rem on the statue delivered (abstract, causa irrelevant); not of the Diana.
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 25] Ago kauft bei der Bildhauerin Bellona eine Diana-Statue. Bei der Abholung gibt ihm Bellona versehentlich eine Penthesilea-Statue; beide merken es nicht. (a) Eigentum an Diana? (b) an Penthesilea? (c) nach Code civil? (d) nach § 929 BGB?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Textbook exercises (Ex 23–28)
cards.front: [Textbook Ex 26] Uncle Felix gives his niece Europa a sealed bag of gold coins; when she asks whether she should pay it back, he says: “We'll talk about that the day after tomorrow.” Felix dies; his heir is Gripus. Can Gripus vindicate the money? What if Europa has already spent it?
cards.back:
The causa is open (gift or loan?) → controversy.
• According to Julian (D 41.1.36): agreement on the essentials (transfer without consideration) suffices → Europa became owner upon the handover → no REI VINDICATIO.
• According to Ulpian (D 12.1.18 pr): no IUSTA CAUSA → ownership remains with the deceased or his heir → REI VINDICATIO by Gripus, as long as the coins are present and distinguishable (sealed bag!).
• Spent/mixed: Europa acquires ownership originally → no vindication, at most a CONDICTIO.
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 26] Onkel Felix gibt seiner Nichte Europa einen versiegelten Beutel Goldmünzen; auf ihre Frage, ob sie zurückzahlen solle: „Darüber reden wir übermorgen.“ Felix stirbt; Erbe ist Gripus. Kann Gripus das Geld vindizieren? Was, wenn Europa es schon ausgegeben hat?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Textbook exercises (Ex 23–28)
cards.front: [Textbook Ex 27] Merops inherits a farm from Omphale and sells and mancipates a cow and a bull to Nastes. Pomona had entrusted the cow to Omphale before going on a journey; the bull belonged jointly to Omphale and her neighbour Lucius. Has Nastes acquired ownership?
cards.back:
Cow: No — Omphale was only a depositary; the heir Merops steps into her position and therefore has neither ownership nor authority of disposal → NEMO PLUS IURIS …; the (abstract) MANCIPATIO is also derivative. Pomona remains owner (usucaption by Nastes may come into consideration — Ch. VIII).
Bull: CONDOMINIUM — Merops could dispose only of Omphale's share → Nastes becomes joint owner of one half alongside Lucius.
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 27] Merops erbt von Omphale einen Hof und verkauft und mancipiert eine Kuh und einen Stier an Nastes. Die Kuh hatte Pomona der Omphale für eine Reise anvertraut; der Stier gehörte Omphale und ihrem Nachbarn Lucius gemeinsam. Eigentum des Nastes?

cards.topic: 27.10. Acquiring ownership I — Textbook exercises (Ex 23–28)
cards.front: [Textbook Ex 28] On 1.1. Cassandra sells a vase to Leo for 1.000; Leo is to pay and collect it in a week. In the meantime Cassandra sells and delivers the vase to Xerxes for 1.500. Who owns the vase — (a) under Roman law, (b) under the ABGB, (c) under the Code civil?
cards.back:
(a) Roman law: Xerxes — sale + delivery (TRADITIO ex iusta causa from the owner); Leo's sale gave him nothing. Leo has only contractual claims against Cassandra.
(b) ABGB: likewise Xerxes (TITULUS + MODUS; only delivery transfers ownership).
(c) Code civil: Leo became owner upon conclusion of the contract; in a double sale of movables, however, the person to whom the thing was delivered first acquires it, if he possesses in good faith (Art 1198 CC) → Xerxes, provided he is in good faith.
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 28] Cassandra verkauft am 1.1. eine Vase um 1.000 an Leo; Leo soll in einer Woche zahlen und abholen. Inzwischen verkauft und übergibt Cassandra die Vase um 1.500 an Xerxes. Wem gehört die Vase — (a) römisch, (b) ABGB, (c) Code civil?
